items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs log best day in about a month, all through IBIT
items.blurb: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $527M on Monday 10-19. BlackRock's IBIT added ~$665M, its biggest day in roughly a year, while Fidelity and Grayscale funds saw outflows.
items.why_matters: A real demand signal after weeks of outflows, but it is concentrated in one fund; a second strong day would confirm it.
items.source: Farside; SoSoValue via briefs.co / The Block (2026-10-20)

items.headline: BTC climbs back toward $83k as oil and yields cool
items.blurb: Bitcoin traded between about $81.2k and $83.2k on Tuesday, ending near $83k. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 5.10% and oil fell on a report of progress toward ending the Iran war.
items.why_matters: Lower yields and oil are the cleanest macro tailwind for BTC right now; $83–84k is the level that would turn the short-term trend up.

items.headline: Iran peace report denied, oil bounces back
items.blurb: WTI dropped toward $95.50 on a report that Qatar and Pakistan had a proposal with preliminary US and Iranian approval, then regained about $2 after the report was denied.
items.why_matters: Oil headlines are still swinging risk assets intraday; a confirmed deal would ease the inflation worry hanging over the Fed.

items.headline: Ether ETFs bleed for a fourth straight day
items.blurb: Spot ether ETFs lost about $103M on Monday, extending a run of withdrawals, while bitcoin funds drew money.
items.why_matters: Institutional money is picking bitcoin over the rest of the market, which keeps ETH and altcoins lagging.

items.headline: Switzerland's FINMA approves its first bitcoin ETF
items.blurb: The Swiss regulator granted an exemption allowing a single-asset bitcoin ETF, citing bitcoin's long trading history and high volume; the issuer was not named.
items.why_matters: Slow-burn access story: another major market opening a regulated bitcoin wrapper supports long-run demand, not this week's price.
